claims.text: An established single-phase HEA is currently used as an intermediate material in plasma-facing reactor components.
Substituting approximately 5 at.% of a principal element with copper will enhance the HEA's heat-transfer capability.
A roughly 5 at.% copper substitution will preserve the HEA's single-phase structural integrity under reactor operating conditions.
Binary-phase-diagram-informed approaches can predict single-solid-solution and multiphase regions in HEAs.
The proposed copper-modified composition lies within a single-phase region predicted by binary phase-diagram analysis.
Temperatures of approximately 600–800°C with cyclic thermal and mechanical loading are typical of plasma-facing reactor operation.
Maintaining a single-phase solid-solution microstructure prevents formation of deleterious secondary phases.
Copper has higher electron thermal conductivity than the unspecified principal element it replaces.
Copper substitution will increase the free-electron contribution to heat conduction in the HEA.
The selected approximately 5 at.% substitution level will preserve phase stability while altering the alloy's electronic structure.
The copper-modified HEA will have approximately 10–20% higher thermal conductivity than the baseline HEA.
The copper-modified HEA will retain yield strength and ductility within approximately 5% of baseline values.
The current intermediate-layer HEA has moderate thermal conductivity and robust structural integrity.
Copper additions above approximately 5 at.% may cause phase separation or deterioration of mechanical properties.
The thermal-conductivity and mechanical-property effects depend on the specific alloy system and processing conditions.
